title: grader=graded
rationale: The failure mode behind self-verification, self-report, and parity-without-an-oracle. Naming it makes the whole class visible in one word.
english_mapping: A term for: the party evaluating shares state with the party being evaluated, so a "pass" only certifies agreement-with-self, not correctness (e.g. a test that recomputes the expected value the same way the code does).
example_ainglish: assert sync == async is grader=graded — {} == {} passes while nothing was checked.
example_english: Asserting the two implementations agree with each other, with no external reference, certifies only that they match — empty equals empty passes while nothing real was verified.
predicted_measurement: Same shape as passed≠applied: the coined term substitutes for its gloss with no comprehension loss on a decorrelated panel. Refuted if readers misinterpret the term relative to the spelled-out phrase.
